priorities: Stop or equal button levels command neutral and clear direction memory.
An opposite-direction request commands neutral for the current scan and clears direction memory.
Otherwise, command the desired direction immediately. After a reversal-neutral scan, evaluate current inputs again; do not retain a pending request.
The one-scan interlock is a command-level function; physical contactor interlocking and safety functions require separate engineering.

initial_values.note: These are pre-invocation values. Scan 0 executes the transition normally.

scan_execution_order.name: Edge sampling
scan_execution_order.action: Sample each input once. All inputs are level-sensitive; no edge detection is required.

scan_execution_order.name: Safety/reset priority and state transitions
scan_execution_order.action: Read previous_direction as the retained pre-state. Set desired_direction to 0 if Stop is true or the button levels are equal, to 1 if only ForwardButton is true, and to -1 if only ReverseButton is true. Apply the state transition table to select output_direction, then store it as previous_direction. Stop clears direction memory but is not latched.

scan_execution_order.name: Unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF
scan_execution_order.action: No timer FBs are required or called; the neutral interval is exactly one invocation.

scan_execution_order.name: Unified output assignments
scan_execution_order.action: Assign Forward := (output_direction = 1) and Reverse := (output_direction = -1) once. Observe these outputs at the end of the same scan.
